subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Classification Trees
description: A short lesson to help you apply Classification Trees.

hook.text: You have 8 input fields, each with 3–5 values. Drawing a tree of classifications makes combinations visible.

buildup.text: A classification tree organizes inputs hierarchically: each branch is a variable, leaves are its values.

discovery.text: Selecting one leaf per branch creates a test case. The tree makes it visual and easy to spot missing combos.

twist.text: Trees get unwieldy with many variables. They work best for 3–8 inputs where visual clarity still helps.

climax.text: Classification Tree Editor (CTE) tools generate test cases from the tree automatically.

punchline.text: See the combinations as a tree. Pick the branches to test.

quiz.question: What does a classification tree help visualize?
options: Input variable combinations for test case design
